result.rationale: The diff adds cook_method and Post#cook returning raw unchanged when cook_method == raw_html. TopicEmbed.import uses PostRevisor to update imported posts (revisor.revise!(user, ...)), and the diff's PostRevisor changes only remove a blank line and add skip_validations to save — it never updates cook_method. So a staff edit to an imported raw_html post persists new raw that Post#cook will return verbatim, un-cooked. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: PostRevisor accepts new raw but never touches cook_method, so staff edits to imported raw_html posts are saved without ever being cooked. A moderator who edits an imported article through the standard editor gets their markdown rendered verbatim as source text (Post#cook returns raw unchanged for raw_html posts), visibly breaking the post after a routine moderation action with no UI path to fix it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Post.cook_method` with a `:raw_html` mode where `Post#cook` returns `raw` and skips the cooking pipeline (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). Imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` (TopicEmbed.import -> PostCreator opts). However, `PostRevisor#revise!`/`update_post` only updates `@post.raw` and saves, and never updates `cook_method` based on the new content. So if an imported `raw_html` post is later edited through the normal revise path (which supplies new_raw), it will remain `:raw_html` and will continue to bypass cooking, causing non-HTML edits (e.g., markdown) to display verbatim.
